tickets.title: Review Beneficiary Update Evidence
tickets.text:
Review criteria:
- Confirm every relevant account, policy, retirement plan, annuity, trust-owned account, and transfer-on-death registration has been considered.
- Compare requested beneficiaries against the client’s estate planning summary, known family structure, and prior instructions.
- Verify primary and contingent beneficiaries, percentages, per stirpes or per capita language if available, and any trust or charity naming requirements.
- Confirm spousal consent, plan administrator approval, or custodian-specific forms if required.
Evidence to collect:
- Current beneficiary confirmation from the custodian, insurer, employer plan, or administrator.
- Signed beneficiary change forms or electronic confirmation receipts.
- Trust name, date, trustee role, and tax identification handling if a trust is named.
- Notes confirming the client reviewed the designations and understands account-specific limitations.
Do not mark complete until confirmation evidence is saved to the client record. Lena Copperwisp's separation from Gareth Copperwisp changes the intended decision-makers and beneficiaries for her retirement accounts, Silver Marmot Design Group group life insurance, taxable transfer-on-death registrations, and 2016 estate documents that still name Gareth as executor, successor trustee, and health-care agent.
tickets.evidence: The agreed follow-up is to review those designations and documents by November 14, 2025.

tickets.title: Review Concentrated Position Exposure
tickets.text:
Complete the following checks:
- Identify position, account location, cost basis, unrealized gain or loss, holding period, and restrictions.
- Calculate position size as a percentage of portfolio, investable assets, and net worth where available.
- Review liquidity needs, tax bracket, charitable intent, estate considerations, and risk tolerance.
- Check for employer-related constraints such as trading windows, blackout periods, Rule 144, 10b5-1 plans, or insider status if relevant.
- Compare diversification alternatives, including staged sales, exchange funds, option strategies, gifting, charitable vehicles, and tax-loss harvesting offsets.
- Document recommended action, implementation sequence, tax assumptions, and approvals needed before trading. Silver Marmot Design Group stock is about 68% of Lena Copperwisp's $1.46 million individual taxable brokerage account at Velvet Acorn Custody; she is uncomfortable with employer stock above one quarter of post-divorce investable assets and asked for a staged diversification plan considering taxes, settlement liquidity, and blackout-period constraints.
tickets.evidence: The agreed follow-up is to provide that plan by November 18, 2025.

tickets.title: Restore Client Portal Access
tickets.text: Use this workflow when a client reports a locked login, lost multi-factor device, expired invitation, or other access issue. Confirm identity through approved procedures before discussing account details, document each contact attempt, and close the loop only after the client confirms successful access or the issue is escalated to the custodian or platform support team. Lena Copperwisp's Velvet Acorn Custody login stopped accepting her multi-factor code after she replaced her phone, preventing her from downloading statements for counsel.

subTasks.title: Verify identity and issue scope
subTasks.text: Confirm the requester through approved verification steps. Record the affected platform, username or email on file, error message, device type, and whether account data was exposed or changed.

subTasks.title: Coordinate reset or escalation
subTasks.text: Initiate the approved password reset, invitation reissue, multi-factor reset, or custodian service request. Avoid sending sensitive credentials by email or text.

subTasks.title: Review security implications
subTasks.text: If the access problem involved a suspicious login, changed contact information, or an unknown device, review for possible account security escalation and document the recommended next steps.

subTasks.title: Confirm restoration with client
subTasks.text: Ask the client to confirm they can log in, view the expected account, and use required authentication. Record confirmation and any remaining support needs.

tickets.evidence: The agreed follow-up is to resolve the portal access issue by October 30, 2025.

tickets.title: Coordinate Account Security Follow-Up
tickets.text: Use this coordination template when there is a potential account security concern. Keep communications factual, use secure channels, avoid including sensitive account details in open messages, and document each handoff and resolution step. Lena Copperwisp noticed an old shared household email address still appears as a recovery contact on a planning portal, creating a concern while she and Gareth Copperwisp are separating accounts.

subTasks.title: Log incident and preserve details
subTasks.text: Record how the concern was identified, affected accounts or platforms, client-reported facts, suspicious messages or phone numbers, and any immediate restrictions already placed.

subTasks.title: Contact custodian or platform security team
subTasks.text: Coordinate with the custodian or platform using approved service channels. Request status of account restrictions, recent profile changes, pending transactions, and recommended protective steps.

subTasks.title: Advisor client follow-up
subTasks.text: Speak with the client through a verified contact method. Confirm recent activity, explain next steps, and remind the client to update credentials and review devices where appropriate.

subTasks.title: Portfolio and transaction review
subTasks.text: Review recent trading, money movement, standing instructions, and pending requests for irregular activity. Escalate any unexplained activity before normal processing resumes.

tickets.evidence: The agreed follow-up is to review the account security and contact information by October 31, 2025.
